name: Home game, ~40bb (loose-passive)
description: Adjusted for a loose-passive home game about 40bb deep: slightly tighter opens (pots go multi-way), bigger open sizes, fewer light 3-bet bluffs and more value 3-bets. 4-bets are effectively all-ins. An approximation — edit anything in the Range Editor.

notes.groups: Seat groups for the limper, squeeze, limp-raise and 4-bet spots: EP (first seats), MP (middle), CO, BTN, SB, BB. More players behind = tighter.
notes.vsLimpers: raise = iso-raise, limp = overlimp (complete from the SB), anything else folds (the big blind checks). Iso-raise hands that play well heads-up with the initiative and dominate limping ranges: pairs, strong broadways, strong suited aces. Overlimp hands that want a cheap multi-way flop: small pairs (sets), suited connectors and suited aces (nut draws), especially late and with more limpers. Fold offsuit hands that flop weak one-pair hands multi-way (KTo, QJo from early seats). The iso range gets tighter as limpers increase (key 3 = 3 or more limpers). Home game 40bb, loose-passive: limpers call iso-raises too often, so iso for value with hands that dominate them (6x+ pairs, strong broadways, strong suited aces) and size up: 4bb + 1bb per limper.
notes.squeeze: An open plus callers before you. Squeeze sizes come from sizing.ts (about 3x the open + 1 open per caller in position, 4x + 1 per caller out of position). Calls favour hands that play well multi-way. Home game: squeeze for value with very few bluffs, because loose-passive players call too much.
notes.vsLimpRaise: You limped and someone raised behind. Limping ranges contain few strong hands, so most limps fold; the calls are hands that play well in a multi-way pot. This spot mostly teaches that limp-calling is weak.
notes.vs4bet: You 3-bet and face a 4-bet. 5bet = all-in. At 40bb a 4-bet commits most of the stack, so it is jam or fold (no flatting).
